# Setup
```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(dpi = 300, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", error = TRUE)

library(here)
library(tidyverse)
library(bioseq)

basedir <- here("species/bflo/genome/VNyyK")
```

# Data

```{r}
fasta_to_tibble <- function(x) {
  x %>% 
    enframe(value = "sequence") %>% 
    mutate(tid = str_replace(name, "(.+?) (.*)", "\\1")) %>% 
    mutate(details = str_replace(name, "(.+?) (.*)", "\\2")) %>% 
    relocate(tid, details) %>% 
    select(-name)
}
```

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| message: false

rfa <- read_fasta(here(basedir, "data/refseq/GCF_000003815.2_Bfl_VNyyK_rna.fna.gz")) %>% 
  fasta_to_tibble()
ids <- read_tsv(here(basedir, "results/genes/gid-tid_mapping.tsv"))
gtf <- read_tsv(here(basedir, "results/gtf/gtf_fixed_parsed.tsv"), 
                col_types = cols(
                  .default = col_character(),
                  start = col_double(),
                  end = col_double(),
                  width = col_double(),
                  exon_number = col_double()
                ))
```

# Check for consistency between GTF and RNA fasta file

- There are fewer transcripts in the RNA fasta file from RefSeq than in the GTF


```{r}
length(unique(rfa$tid))
length(unique(gtf$transcript_id))
length(unique(ids$transcript_id))
```

- But all the transcripts missing from the fasta are tRNA transcripts

```{r}
gtf %>% 
  filter(!transcript_id %in% rfa$tid &
           !is.na(transcript_id) &
           gbkey %in% c("mRNA", "ncRNA", "tRNA", "rRNA")) %>% 
  select(seqnames, source, type, gene_id, transcript_id, gbkey, symbol) %>% 
  distinct() %>% 
  pull(gbkey) %>% 
  unique()
```

- There are three transcripts that are in the fasta file but not in the GTF file
- I looked up all three transcripts on NCBI and they are all from pseudogenes

```{r}
rfa$tid[!rfa$tid %in% gtf$transcript_id]
```

# Conclusion

This means tha the RNA fasta from RefSeq is almost entirely consistent with the fixed GTF file. We can simply use that fasta file to generate an index for `kallisto`.
